criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose, rationale, single-spacecraft justification and users (operator/customers) all addressed with literature references. Some user detail is speculative ('likely'), but overall strong.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major elements covered with STK screenshots and access table. But launch choice is speculative (Vega E not yet built), RAAN 27.33° is inconsistent with Kourou launch site, no hand calcs for inclination, and EOL text is truncated. Errors reduce persuasiveness.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved
The proposed ZYZZsat is small and without thrusters in a low-earth orbit.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarises design and notes launch risk, but is largely generic recap without quantitative outcomes or critical assessment.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure and headings are logical, but references are bare URLs with OCR/typo artefacts, Wikipedia used as a source, figures partly unlabelled, and some writing errors. Not professional level.

evidence.quote: a wiki sorted directory – ‘Timeline of spaceflight’ – will be referred to throughout the report [6].

technical_issues.issue: RAAN of 27.33° is inconsistent with a Kourou (5°N) launch into a 97.79° SSO; RAAN depends on launch time, not launch site latitude.
Inclination 97.7924° for 600 km SSO is plausible but no hand calculation shown; only a plotted curve.
Selecting Vega E (first flight 2024, unbuilt) is speculative; no mass/payload compatibility or cost analysis.
Access table has duplicate row 15 and a mislabelled row 6 date; mean duration stated as ~10 min but table mean is 580.8 s (~9.7 min) — minor.
EOL paragraph truncated ('utilising a large surface area to ‘'); no quantitative deorbit time or drag-sail sizing.
Claim that a high altitude yields 'low resolution images which is also desirable' is a wording/logic error.

overall: A competent, well-structured mission design covering most requirements with STK evidence, but weakened by speculative launch choice, an inconsistent RAAN, missing hand calculations, truncated EOL discussion, and poor referencing including Wikipedia. Adequate overall.

feedback.summary: A competent, well-structured mission design that covers most requirements with STK evidence and a clear mission rationale. To reach the next level, tighten the orbital analysis (RAAN consistency, hand calculations), justify the launch vehicle with data, complete the EOL discussion, and professionalise referencing and figures.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly states the mission purpose, the single-spacecraft rationale and the users, with literature support. To reach the top of Accomplished, firm up the user discussion (avoid 'likely') and cite specific operator/customer commitments rather than speculative wording.
criteria.C2: You cover all major design elements with STK screenshots and an access table, but several errors weaken persuasiveness. The RAAN of 27.33° is inconsistent with a Kourou launch into a 97.79° SSO; the Vega E choice is speculative with no mass/cost analysis; no hand calculation supports the 97.7924° inclination; and the EOL paragraph is truncated. Fix these and add quantitative evidence to move from Adequate to Accomplished.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion recaps the design and flags launch risk, but remains a generic summary. To reach Accomplished, state quantitative outcomes (orbit, contact frequency, lifetime) and critically assess trade-offs and residual risks against the evidence in the main body.
criteria.C4: Headings and structure are logical, but referencing is not professional: bare URLs, Wikipedia as a source, and inconsistent citation formatting. Figures are partly unlabelled and some writing errors remain. To reach Accomplished, use a consistent citation style, replace Wikipedia with primary sources, label all figures/tables, and proofread.

next_steps: Recompute and justify the RAAN for your Kourou launch time, and add a hand calculation for the 97.7924° SSO inclination to support the STK plot.
Replace the Vega E with a flown vehicle or provide payload mass, cost and schedule evidence; complete the EOL section with a quantitative deorbit time and drag-sail sizing.

Rebuild the bibliography in a consistent style using primary sources (no Wikipedia or bare URLs), label every figure and table, and proofread for wording errors such as the 'low resolution images' claim.
